evidence:
Scope: tests/app_context.md plus the five tests/*/*/prompt.md of the frozen task. Hashes of all six files and instruction.md recomputed and equal to manifest.json; the six files are byte-identical to the current project copies. Static review only: no configured judge run exists for this candidate (raw-evidence-index scope says full configured grading is absent; its 10 artifact hashes all recompute correctly), and this row does not need one.

WHAT IS ACCURATE (checked, not assumed):
1. Identity/URL: app_context.md:3-4 'Name: HireOps', 'URL: http://localhost:3000'; all five prompts open http://localhost:3000 (6 occurrences in tests, no other host/port). Matches instruction.md:15 (port 3000) and integration.md.
2. Accounts: app_context.md:8-16 lists exactly the seven emails and password `Hireops!2026` of instruction.md:19; names, emails, roles and approver tiers 1/2/3 equal seed_data.json users (authority_tier 1/2/3 for Sorensen/Okafor/Tanaka). No other email address, domain or password appears in any prompt or judge.toml (grep of all emails/passwords: each of the 7 once, in app_context only; prompts inherit it via {app_context} as the staged contract requires).
3. Screens/entities: app_context.md:20 names six screens matching instruction.md:5's six views; visual/prompt.md:14 lists the same six; functional/prompt.md:53 'all six screens'. Entities used by prompts (requisition, PENDING/COMMITTED/DRAFT offer, grant, signing remittance, referral accrual, change set/preview/receipt, operation key) are all defined in hireops_rules.md sections 1-12. 'Dara' and 'all three supplied referrers' (functional P1/P4) match seed employees (Dara Whitfield, Sofia Marchetti, Omar Haddad); 'imported DRAFT offers' (P9) matches the one DRAFT seed offer and rules line 216; 'one Finance actor' (B5) matches the seed.
4. Reference moment 2026-08-01T00:00:00Z (app_context.md:27) equals rules line 60 and seed; anchor split (referral vs rescission effective date) matches rules lines 63-67.
5. Every numeric expectation in the functional prompt was recomputed from the rules and constants and is correct: P3 intrinsic .02/annualized .01/run-rate base+.01/basis base+.02 and bands 1/2/2/3 (bases 199999.97, 199999.98, 349999.97, 349999.98); P4 intrinsic 7.07/22.11/39.13, annualized 1.77/5.53/9.78, run-rate 100001.77/110005.53/90009.78, basis 105001.78/114005.55/96009.81, signing 10000.01/-1999.98/+4000.02, rescission 12 months, 4800.02 vested/7200.03 clawed, 3 retained/10 cancelled; P6 headroom 39.75; P7 13 months 45%/24%, 24 months 100%/68%, 32 months 100%/100%; P8 10000/5000/10000 and 5000+5000 contingent; B1 run-rates 100.00 and adjustments -1.98/+2.04; D1 basis 105.01->104.02 and 105.01->106.03 and -0.01 overrun at base 94.48; P2 90071992547409.91 dollars = 9007199254740991 cents (max safe), B2 overflow control. Status codes 401/403/409 match rules sections 8 and 11.
6. Internal references resolve: criteria ids named in prompts exist (hro_anon_read_status, hro_keep_revision_terms, hro_keep_rescission_date in functional/judge.toml; hro_pol_change_recovery in polish/judge.toml). Every protocol label used by functional criteria (P1-P10, P5a, B1-B6, D1-D4, L1-L3, E1, R1, R2) is defined in functional/prompt.md, and none is referenced that the prompt lacks. The polish prompt's 'live-update / ended-session / focus / lost-response' rows map to the five polish criteria. restart_app is wired in functional/judge.toml (verifier MCP server) and the prompt restricts it to P10.
7. Residue: grep of the six files for CHANGE_ME, TODO/FIXME, sibling product names (Colderwater etc.), tenant/invoice/ticket/patient/inventory vocabulary and foreign email domains found nothing (the only hits were the legitimate phrase 'read family' matched by a loose pattern). No template placeholder survives. Deliverable description (desktop transaction workspace, no phone layout or theme switching, empty operational desk allowed) in render criterion, visual/prompt.md:12-14 and app_context.md:21 matches instruction.md:5 and :17.

INSTANCES REPORTED (none misdescribes the app or changes a verdict; all P3):
I1. tests/scored/polish/prompt.md:16, last sentence: 'Successful scripted setup is not configured-judge workload evidence.' This is an authoring/QC-process statement (it paraphrases qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md 'Scripted Playwright duration is not LLM judge duration'), not an instruction about this app or about grading. It is residue from review work inside a judge prompt.
I2. tests/app_context.md:20 names the screens 'Equity Table' and 'Audit Trail', whereas instruction.md:5 asks for 'Equity' and 'Audit' views and says 'the layout and names are yours'. 'Equity Table'/'Audit Trail' are the reference solution's navigation labels (solution/app/public/js/app.js lines 17 and 19); 'Audit Trail' is also used by hireops_rules.md:387/409, 'Equity Table' is not public. Mitigated by app_context.md:28-31 ('any route layout and suitable labels ... never assume the reference implementation's private routes, selectors'), so a conforming app labelled 'Equity' is not failed.
I3. tests/app_context.md:12-14 call the approvers 'tier 1/2/3' while instruction.md:19 calls the same accounts 'Approver, Band I/II/III'. Rules lines 41-42 and 164-165 equate them ('tier-3 (Band III) approver'), and seed stores authority_tier, so the context is accurate; only the wording differs between brief and judge context.
I4. tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:3 says 'Use restart_app only once, at P10's end', but P10 (line 57) and hro_restart place the single restart in the middle of P10, followed by re-reads and the post-restart retry. Line 57 also says 'Restart LAST, after B protocols' while the D/L/E/R protocols are written after it (lines 75-97); D and L are embedded in B, but E1, R1 and R2 are standalone, so their position relative to the restart is unstated. Harmless for correctness (data must survive restart either way) but the two sentences are not literally consistent.
I5. tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:93 and criterion hro_entries_reload say 'Switch to another workspace and back' where every other place calls these 'views'/'screens' (the golden's code calls them workspaces). Wording only.
I6. tests/scored/polish/prompt.md:16 tells the Polish judge to 'record the separate Functional failure'; a Polish judge has no channel to record a Functional verdict. It reads as intended ('do not score freshness here'), so no wrong score follows.
counterexample: None that changes a score was found. Broken app that could pass because of a prompt inaccuracy: none identified; credentials, URL, screens and expected figures in the prompts are those of the public brief and rules. Conforming alternative that could fail: an app labelling its screens 'Equity' and 'Audit' (exactly as the brief words them) was considered against I2; app_context.md:28-31 tells the judge to accept suitable labels, so it is not failed.
suggested_fix: Optional clean-up in a new candidate: delete the sentence 'Successful scripted setup is not configured-judge workload evidence.' from tests/scored/polish/prompt.md:16; name the screens 'Equity' and 'Audit' in app_context.md:20 as the brief does; change functional/prompt.md:3 to 'Use restart_app only once, inside P10' and state that P10 follows all B/D/L/E/R protocols. Any such edit invalidates this clearance and needs re-review.
